governing: angle shear rupture of the net section (AISC 360-22 J4.2b), sa1/steel.shear_rupture
notes: Petra PASS (identical to try2.petra): 15 of 15 obligations certified for ASD shear 0 to 39.449 kip. Design: one L4x4x1/4 A36 angle, 13-1/8 in long, with 4 rows of 7/8 in A325-N (threads included, snug, standard holes) at 3 in pitch on each leg; Lev 2-1/16 in; gauge 2 in on both legs (toe edges 2 in); top bolt 3-5/8 in below the beam top, so the angle starts 1-9/16 in down, below kdet (1-7/16 in); beam setback 1/2 in, beam end distance 1-1/2 in. Bolt groups are checked by the elastic method with eccentricity on both legs (beam side e = 2 in, support side e = 2 in + tw/2). Closest margins: shear rupture 0.994, which fixes the minimum angle length; block shear on 4 rows 0.968; bolt tearout to the angle edge 0.947 on the support side. The 13-1/8 in length is the shortest a 1/4 in angle can be with four 7/8 in bolts, so do not shorten it or change Lev. Hand checks agree with Petra. Petra does not check: (1) tearout of the beam web toward the beam end under the horizontal bolt-force component (7.9 kip against a 12.0 kip allowable, or about 23.6 kip measured along the resultant, so it is fine by J3.11); (2) shear-flexure interaction in the angle (0.835^2 + 0.374^2 = 0.83); (3) the Manual's flexibility and ductility practice for connection angles. A 1/4 in angle is the most flexible choice. The beam-fit check uses kdes, but the angle also clears kdet. Petra checks the design; a licensed engineer still has to review and sign it.
